engagement_background.objective: Cascade Residential Services engaged Treya Partners to capture $0.87–$1.7 million in annual cost savings through strategic sourcing, leverage the company’s enterprise-wide buying power, and build a best-in-class procurement process that drives an estimated $16.6 million in enterprise-value creation within a 5- to 6-month window.
engagement_background.scope_summary: The project initially covers nine spend categories—HVACR OEM/distributors, HVACR & plumbing supplies, advertising, general industrial/electrical supplies, electronic payment processing, telecom (data & voice), fleet, uniforms, and commercial print—representing $32.9 M in baseline spend of which $26.5 M (≈80%) is addressable; low-value categories may be dropped or recategorised as analysis progresses.
constraints_challenges: Supplier data responsiveness: obtaining line-item usage data from key vendors can be slow or incomplete.
Decentralised purchasing across multiple business units limits leverage and complicates stakeholder alignment.
Incumbent supplier sensitivities and potential pushback during competitive bidding or negotiations.
Stakeholder time constraints and the need for timely feedback to keep the aggressive 5–6-month timeline on track.
Risk of side conversations or parallel sourcing efforts by business units that could undermine a unified negotiation strategy.

procurement_environment.data_availability: One year of AP header-level data (Jan–Dec 2024) is available; detailed usage data must be requested from high-spend suppliers; contracts are scattered across business units.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Spend mis-categorisation (e.g., commercial print) and inconsistent vendor naming; line-item history may be missing where suppliers do not respond, requiring representative samples for baselining.
